verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's API access tokens docs say tokens can be scoped to restrict the operations they can perform, for example a read-only integration. That directly supports issuing least-privilege credentials an agent could use, and role assignment docs add custom roles that override base permissions. Missing for 10: agent- or MCP-specific guidance tying scoped tokens to agent use, detail on how fine-grained scoping goes (per-project, per-environment, expiry), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You can scope your API tokens to restrict the set of operations they can perform. For example, you can build an integration that only has read access
If a member is directly assigned a role, such as a preset role or a role that you create, that role is used instead of the member's base role
